Expectations — 1 of 2

"What CTC are you expecting?"

I'm aiming for a monthly take-home salary between Rs.75–80k. I feel that this is an appropriate amount, given:

  • My breadth of experience and achievements, which you can read about in greater detail .
  • Mumbai's insane cost-of-living, which makes anything less than the quoted range impractical.
  • The fact that I need to support my aunt (who I live with in Mumbai) financially, especially since she's nearing retirement.
Note that this range is carefully-considered. If this is a dealbreaker, then .

Expectations — 2 of 2

"Any other expectations we should know about?"

  • I likely won't join any place beyond Andheri (to my south) or Borivali (to my north), given rush-hour commute times from where I live (Malad West).
  • I'd appreciate having the option to work remotely on certain days/weeks (for example, if I'm ill or visiting home). However, given my experiences during COVID, I largely prefer working in offices to remote working.
  • I'm looking to work as part of a TEAM: a team that is passionate, energetic, collaborative and accepting of interpersonal differences. I've done enough of siloed, close-minded workplaces till now.

Additional Questions — 2 of 8

"What would you say are some of your biggest weaknesses?"

  • I can occasionally be quite arrogant and stubborn. However, given my experience as a supervisor (involving compromise and dealing with impossible deadlines), I like to think that I've worked on this significantly, and that 2019 me would be shocked at the sheer pragmatism of 2026 me.
  • I'm not sociable: in fact, I'm quite introverted and shy. Many might (and often do) misconstrue this as rudeness. This is something I've worked on significantly, and I'm confident that once you get to know me better, this will cease to be a major issue. Also, and this goes without saying, I've NEVER let this intrude on my work in terms of collaborations, responsiveness, and especially client calls/meetings/presentations.
  • While I'm as able as anyone else when it comes to working with trends in pop culture if needed, I do not follow it religiously (let alone buy into it). If it wasn't apparent from whatever you might have read about me thus far, I'm very much both a nerd and a hipster. It is what it is, and I feel that this disconnect allows me to approach projects I'm put on from unique, productive perspectives.
  • My written Hindi (my third language) is beyond abysmal, at least without the help of AI. My spoken Hindi is worth a chuckle or two, though.
† I abuse parentheses (a LOT).

Additional Questions — 3 of 8

"Impressive skill range, but none of it is unique. What value do you add that others don't?"

My skills are genuine — honed pre-AI, through years of trial and error.
  • There's a reason I've used "pre-AI" or "pre-GPT" throughout this website: my skills are genuine, honed through years of trial and error since I've never studied marketing or related fields in college. In addition to this, I'm still versatile enough to use AI platforms to aid and bolster my work far more effectively than most others.
  • Remember when I called myself "stubborn"? That's also an asset of mine. I NEVER give up and seldom stop until a task or project is satisfactorily done.
  • Given my OCD, I'm a massive stickler for grammar. Test this for yourself: find any grammatical errors or inconsistencies on this website (written, again, without the aid of AI). You'd think that fields like copywriting would naturally attract such types, but surprisingly, I've encountered only a handful of them. I'm also particularly adept at recognising AI-isms in text.
  • According to my coworkers, I tend to create the impression of being an "intellectual" in the way that I speak. While the people who sincerely believe this have probably never met an actual intellectual, it has come in quite handy in impressing difficult clients.

Additional Questions — 4 of 8

"Why advertising, by the way? Why not engineering, since that's what you'd studied in college?"

Enrolling in an engineering course was not my decision. My parents, being scientists themselves, felt that studying engineering (or medicine) was the safest career choice for me to make. However, I was never really good at it because it never interested me. Writing has always been my calling and marketing provided an opportunity to harness that for an actual living, as opposed to being a creative writer (which doesn't pay unless you're Chetan Bhagat), or a journalist (which is not only a dying field in the age of social media, but also requires qualifications I didn't study for).

Additional Questions — 6 of 8

"What are you expecting from your time here? Anything you're looking to learn in particular?"

Note that the following are not dealbreakers for me, but they'd be great to have:

  • I'd like the opportunity to work on a proper, big-budget DVC or TVC for once.
  • Some mentorship/guidance would be great when it comes to managing and senior-level decisions (something I didn't really have before).
  • I look forward to working on brands that have the guts/budget to actually execute what they love when pitched.
  • Most importantly, I'd love to learn brand strategy properly: something I've only scratched at with certain pitches.
  • Wishful thinking, but I'd love to work on music-related brands/projects, if possible.

Additional Questions — 7 of 8

"OK, let me rephrase: where do you see yourself in the next 5 years?"

I see myself, hopefully, working here as a Creative Director with:

  • A team that's happy with me and (most importantly) not burnt out themselves.
  • The ability to conceive of campaigns and see them through from start to finish, including (most importantly) strategy.
  • The ability to inspire even greater confidence in clients through my presentation skills (and the ability to sell them anything).
  • Even more prestigious awards under our belt (perhaps including a Cannes Lion win!).
  • A daily morning commute past billboards with one of our ads on it.
  • My YouTube viewings interrupted by DVCs I've worked on (as long as we're dreaming).
  • More-than-amicable relationships with everyone else; no bridges burnt.
  • A decent work-life balance despite all of this.

Additional Questions — 8 of 8

"One last thing: why the gaps between jobs?"

  • Between my first and second jobs (2021): Chalk it up to lockdown-induced burnout and depression.
  • Between my second and last jobs (2022): I'd gone home after three years — the longest I'd stayed away — and thus needed time to reconnect. I was still working then, albeit as a freelancer for my first company.
  • After my last job (2026): I needed some time off to address some serious personal issues before jumping back in. This is probably the last time I'll be able to take such an extended break from the grind, given that I'm in my thirties now.
